# faraday_trait (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "faraday_trait" "tenure" {
  name = "tenure"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) How to refer to this Trait in other API calls to Faraday.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Information about this field.
- `literate` (String) A more human-consumable version of the name of this field.
- `lookup_table` (String) A mapping of the input values used in modeling, to how they should be displayed in reports. Free-form; supply JSON via jsonencode().
- `statistical_type` (String) A string describing the nature of data represented by the trait. categorical_nominal: the field contains one value of an unordered bounded set. Example: "preferred_channel" — one of "email", "sms", "direct_mail". categorical_ordinal: the field contains one value of an ordered bounded set. Example: "spending_tier" — one of "low", "medium", "high", "premium". multicategorical_nominal: the field contains one or more values of an unordered bounded set. Example: "interests" — "outdoors", "travel", "fitness". continuous_ordinal: the field contains numeric values with a natural ordering. Example: "lifetime_value". binary: the field contains boolean-like values representing presence/absence. Example: "has_pool" — true or false. count: the field contains non-negative integer counts. Example: "children_count" — 0, 1, 2, 3. interval: the field contains numeric values where differences are meaningful but ratios are not. Example: "date_of_birth" as epoch. ratio: the field contains numeric values where both differences and ratios are meaningful, with a true zero. Example: "age" — 0, 25, 50. Type compatibility (new values only): - continuous_ordinal requires a numeric type (long, float, double). - categorical_nominal requires string or boolean. - categorical_ordinal requires string. - multicategorical_nominal requires array_of_strings. Deprecated values (still accepted, will be removed in a future version): categorical: equivalent to categorical_nominal. multicategorical: equivalent to multicategorical_nominal. ordinal: ambiguous — prefer categorical_ordinal or continuous_ordinal. nominal: ambiguous — prefer categorical_nominal.
- `unit` (String) For numeric types, in what units is the data stored.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) (For user traits only) If not null, this resource will no longer receive updates, but will still be visable.
- `breaks` (List of Number) For continuous data types, list of reasonable cutoff values.
- `categories` (List of String) For STRING type, list of allowed values.
- `category` (String) A broad category describing the flavor of a trait.
- `coverage` (Number) The percentage (0.1 meaning 10%) of the population for which we know the trait value.
- `created_at` (String) When this resource was created.
- `deprecated` (Boolean) (For Faraday traits only) This trait will no longer receive updated data. Please use the updated version of the trait instead, if available.
- `emitted_by_datasets` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--emitted_by_datasets))
- `id` (String) A unique ID for this resource.
- `permissions` (List of String) What the account is able to use this trait for. Contact support to change access.
- `precision` (String) Precision refers to the specificity used to assign a trait. For example, 'person' precision indicates a trait specific to an individual, such as a preference for baseball, while 'address' precision pertains to a characteristic related to a location, such as the number of bedrooms in a house.
- `resource_type` (String) The type of a resource which is available via the REST SDK.
- `status` (String) The current state of this resource and any updates.
- `tier` (String) A broad category describing the flavor of a trait.
- `type` (String) The data type of a column in table, or of a trait. Types are expressed using a subset of [Avro](https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html). Possible values include: - boolean: A Boolean value. - long: A 64-bit integer. - double: A 64-bit float. - string: A Unicode string, possibly representing categorical data. - date: A date with no reference to time of day.
- `updated_at` (String) When this resource was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--emitted_by_datasets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `emitted_by_datasets`

Read-Only:

- `dataset_id` (String) The dataset the column comes from.
- `parsing` (Attributes) How well this input's declared `format` read the column's values. One report, because one input reads one column. Omitted when the input declares no `format` — there is then nothing that can fail to read — and for traits last built before this was reported. Neither case means every value was read. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--emitted_by_datasets--parsing))

<a id="nestedatt--emitted_by_datasets--parsing"></a>
### Nested Schema for `emitted_by_datasets.parsing`

Read-Only:

- `candidate_row_count` (Number) Rows of the dataset available to this trait.
- `examples` (List of String) A sample of the values that could not be read, to compare against the declared format.
- `parsed_row_count` (Number) Populated rows whose value could be read as the declared format. Divided by `populated_row_count` this is the read rate, which should be 100%; any shortfall means the values and the declared format disagree, and those rows contribute no value to the trait.
- `populated_row_count` (Number) Candidate rows where the column held a value. An empty column is not a failure to read one.
- `stale_before` (String) The date those rows were judged against: anything earlier was counted as implausible. The bound is relative to when the trait was built, so it is reported rather than left to be recalculated against a different day. Present only when rows were actually counted.
- `stale_examples` (List of String) A sample of the values that were read successfully but resolved to an implausible date. These never appear in `examples`, because nothing went wrong when reading them.
- `stale_row_count` (Number) Rows whose value was read successfully but produced a date too far in the past to be plausible, which usually means the format is being misread. Unlike an event stream, a trait does not exclude these rows — the implausible value is kept and used. The count is reported so a misread format is visible rather than silently shaping a model feature.
